SHOT: Worn ring frame, 4:5: the BACK OF ONE HAND held up flat and square to camera in front of the collarbone, fingers together and relaxed, the camera brought close so the ring on the ring finger is legible at its true small size.

CROP: The frame is cut straight across just ABOVE THE UPPER LIP. NO eyes, NO eyebrows, NO forehead anywhere in this picture. Inside the frame: hand, fingers, wrist, collarbone and shoulder.

THE PRODUCT: IMAGE 1 is our approved packshot of this exact piece and the ONLY authority on what it is: copy its construction, proportions, metal colour and stone colour EXACTLY; ignore its cube and its background. IMAGE 1 is a close view, so the piece's SIZE in this picture comes ONLY from the SCALE TEST below. IMAGE 2 is the authority on the model, skin, garment, hair, ground and light: match it exactly, but she wears ONLY the piece from IMAGE 1, worn on the ring finger only, ALL FOUR bands together on that one finger as one stack, the plain band lying directly against the others, never on another finger; the hand is held FLAT against the upper chest below the collarbone, the BACK of the hand square to the camera and the fingers together pointing up, the fingertips at the base of the throat, well BELOW the chin; never touching the chin, the jaw or the mouth; the nose is never in the frame; on the finger FOUR stripes show, in this order from the fingertip side: the slim plain gold band, the gold band of green squares, the silver band of green baguettes, the wide gold band with spaced round stones; nothing else on the bands; any other jewellery in IMAGE 2 is removed.

THE PLATE: A young Indian woman, late twenties, warm mid-brown skin with golden undertones. Long dark brown hair in loose natural waves. Bare shoulders, marigold-saffron silk camisole with narrow spaghetti straps. Nails short, bare, pale nude, no polish colour. Warm cream seamless with a gentle gradient falloff, never sand, tan, beige or golden. Soft large key from camera-left, one soft shadow.

CONSTRUCTION LOCK: AN INTERLOCKED STACK RING: three stone-set bands stacked tightly side by side as one broad ring, with a FOURTH slim plain band threaded through them: (1) a slim gold tone band about 3mm wide with a channel of small square-cut EMERALD-GREEN stones set edge to edge, between two gold rails; (2) a SILVER tone band about 3mm wide with a channel of small rectangular BAGUETTE-cut EMERALD-GREEN stones set end to end, between two bright silver rails; (3) the WIDEST band, a broad flat polished gold tone band about 5mm wide, clearly about twice as wide as each of the others, with about six small round EMERALD-GREEN stones sunk FLUSH into its flat surface, spaced apart, with no raised settings and no claws; (4) a slim plain polished gold tone band about 2mm wide threaded through the stack: off the finger it stands upright across the top of the stack like a ring threaded through a ring, as the packshot shows; WORN, it lies around the SAME finger directly beside the others as a fourth plain stripe, never standing up, never on another finger. Stacked, the three stone bands make one ring about 11mm wide. The silver band ALWAYS carries its green baguette channel, never plain silver; the gold channel band carries small squares and the wide band spaced rounds; a deep blue-green emerald, never grass green, never teal, never black; no white dots or accent stones between the channel stones; never a single band.

SCALE TEST: On the finger the stacked bands cover about 11mm, about two thirds of the finger segment, never wider than the finger. The jewellery keeps its true small size against the body; it is read by bringing the camera closer, never by making the piece bigger.

ABSENCE LIST: No eyes, no eyebrows, no forehead. No second piece of jewellery, no watch, no other rings, no other earrings, no necklace unless it is the product. No nail polish colour. No props, no flowers. Metal: polished gold tone and bright silver tone exactly where IMAGE 1 shows them. No lettering, no watermark, no logo, no tag, no size sticker anywhere in frame. The picture runs edge to edge as a crisp, clean, modern digital studio photograph, shot today on a high-resolution digital camera.

SHOT: Worn ring frame, 4:5: the BACK OF ONE HAND held up flat and square to camera in front of the collarbone, fingers together and relaxed, the camera brought close so the ring on the ring finger is legible at its true small size.

CROP: The frame is cut straight across just ABOVE THE UPPER LIP. NO eyes, NO eyebrows, NO forehead anywhere in this picture. Inside the frame: hand, fingers, wrist, collarbone and shoulder.

THE PRODUCT: IMAGE 1 is the owner's own phone photograph of this exact ring worn on a finger: it is the authority on the ring's SIZE against the finger and on how it sits: the marquise about two thirds of the finger's width, lying ACROSS the finger, and the molten bar about one and a half finger widths long, lying ACROSS the finger beside it; copy exactly that size against the finger, and ignore the tray, the background and the light of IMAGE 1. IMAGE 2 is our approved packshot of the same ring: the authority on its construction, metal colour and stone. IMAGE 3 is the authority on the model, skin, garment, hair, ground and light: match it exactly, but she wears ONLY the ring, on the RING finger only, the fourth finger from the thumb; the marquise and the molten bar both lie ACROSS that finger, side by side and parallel, the bar's one end over the neighbouring finger; any other jewellery in IMAGE 3 is removed.

THE PLATE: A young Indian woman, late twenties, warm mid-brown skin with golden undertones. Long dark brown hair in loose natural waves. Bare shoulders, marigold-saffron silk camisole with narrow spaghetti straps. Nails short, bare, pale nude, no polish colour. Warm cream seamless with a gentle gradient falloff, never sand, tan, beige or golden. Soft large key from camera-left, one soft shadow.

CONSTRUCTION LOCK: AN OPEN TOI-ET-MOI RING made of ONE slim polished gold band about 1.5mm wide that does NOT close. The band's two open ends sit side by side on top of the finger, and BOTH run in the SAME direction as the band itself, around the finger. At one end ONE large clear MARQUISE-cut faceted stone is set LENGTHWISE along the band in four gold claws, its long axis following the band, with the slim band running down its side like a rail. The band's other end becomes ONE long molten gold BAR: a smooth organic rod about 2.5mm thick, slightly wavy, with rounded droplet ends, continuing the line of the band and about two and a half times as long as the marquise. So the marquise and the bar lie side by side and parallel, both in line with the band; on the finger both lie ACROSS the finger. Exactly one stone, a clear marquise, never round, oval or pear; no pave, no halo; the bar is smooth polished gold with soft ripples, never a straight machined bar, never set with stones; the band does not close. The band NEVER crosses behind the marquise and the bar at right angles: never a cross or plus shape, never a straight rod running left to right behind them.

SCALE TEST: On the finger the marquise is about HALF the finger's width, a little shorter than that finger's nail is wide; the bar is about one and a quarter finger widths long, two and a half times the marquise; neither is ever larger, and the ring never covers more than its one finger and part of the neighbouring one. The jewellery keeps its true small size against the body; it is read by bringing the camera closer, never by making the piece bigger.

ABSENCE LIST: No eyes, no eyebrows, no forehead. No second piece of jewellery, no watch, no other rings, no other earrings, no necklace unless it is the product. No nail polish colour. No props, no flowers. Metal: warm 18k gold tone, never brassy, orange or greenish. No lettering, no watermark, no logo, no tag, no size sticker anywhere in frame. The picture runs edge to edge as a crisp, clean, modern digital studio photograph, shot today on a high-resolution digital camera.

SHOT: Extreme macro, 4:5, of ONE stud: the blush octagon stone and its fine gold claws; the stone's outline a REGULAR octagon like a STOP sign, its four diagonal sides exactly as long as its four straight sides, so it reads almost round, never a square with clipped corners, resting on the top face of a cream plaster cube. Camera very close; the piece fills about two thirds of the frame; razor-sharp on the stones and the metal edges, the rest falling softly out of focus.

THE PRODUCT: IMAGE 1 is our approved packshot of this exact piece and the ONLY authority on what it is: copy its construction, proportions, metal colour and stone colour EXACTLY; ignore its cube and its background. IMAGE 1 is a close view, so the piece's SIZE in this picture comes ONLY from the SCALE TEST below. IMAGE 2 is the authority for the plaster, the background and the light only.

CONSTRUCTION LOCK: A PAIR OF OCTAGON SOLITAIRE STUDS: each stud is ONE OCTAGON-cut faceted stone, a REGULAR octagon with eight EQUAL straight sides (the four diagonal sides as long as the four straight ones), so it reads almost round, in a soft BLUSH PINK with peachy flashes, held in a slim gold setting with fine claws at its corners, on a single post. Exactly one stone per stud; a regular octagon with eight equal sides, never a square with small clipped corners, never Asscher, never round, never a hexagon; soft blush pink, never hot pink, never red, never lilac; no halo, no pave.

SCALE TEST: Each stone is about 9.5mm across, about half an earlobe.

LIGHT: Soft large key from camera-left, one soft shadow, plus ONE small hard specular kicker from the right, so the metal shows a bright moving highlight and a dark rolled edge on every curve, and every stone shows internal sparkle and a hard white point, never flat colour.

ABSENCE LIST: No hand, no ear, no model, no fabric, no props. No second piece of jewellery. Only ONE earring is in this picture: its partner from the pair is NOT in frame, no second post, no second stone. Metal: warm 18k gold tone, never brassy, orange or greenish. No lettering, no watermark, no logo, no tag, no size sticker anywhere in frame. The picture runs edge to edge as a crisp, clean, modern digital studio photograph, shot today on a high-resolution digital camera.
